answer.rationale: Finance demands 18% cost reduction AND the contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew, while the line is at 94% with no buffer. Switching vendors (memory_c2) cuts cost but re-introduces onboarding risk we cannot absorb right now. Adding a second source (memory_c3) hedges risk but doesn't address the cost mandate within this single decision slot. Deferring (memory_c5) is not viable with a hard 14-day expiry. The best single lever is to renew with the incumbent on a multi-year commitment (memory_c6 shows this unlocked volume pricing without narrowing scope) while simultaneously benchmarking against market rates to negotiate both price and payment terms (memory_c4 shows this recovered real margin). One decision—negotiate_terms—executed as a renewal-with-multi-year-lock-in at benchmarked pricing, satisfies the cost mandate through volume pricing and improved terms while preserving delivery continuity (memory_c1) and avoiding the migration risk the 94%-utilization line cannot tolerate. Pulling memory_c6 to confirm the multi-year mechanism and the magnitude of the unit-cost reduction before committing.
